title: Fabrication and Characterization of Layer-By-Layer Janus Base Nano-Matrix to Promote Cartilage Regeneration
protocol: Prepare the JBNt monomer using previously published methods.
Purify the crude JBNt monomer with high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) using a reverse-phase column.
Use solvent A: 100% water, solvent B: 100% acetonitrile, and solvent C: HCl water solution at pH = 1 for HPLC purification.
Maintain a flow rate of 3 mL/min during the HPLC process.
Collect the largest peak obtained in the HPLC run at 7.2 minutes.
Add 8 µL of 1 mg/mL TGF-β1 suspended in H2O to 32 µL of 1 mg/mL matrilin-3 suspended in H2O.
Mix thoroughly by pipetting the TGF-β1 and matrilin-3 solutions.
Add 80 µL of 1 mg/mL JBNts suspended in H2O to the TGF-β1/matrilin-3 solution.
Blend the mixture repeatedly by pipetting to ensure proper mixing.
Observe the formation of white floccules indicating the creation of the JBNm.
Add 5 μL of 1 mg/mL JBNts to 50 μL of H2O to make a 90.9 μg/mL solution for the JBNt group.
Add 40 μL of 10 μg/mL matrilin-3 to 15 μL of H2O to make a 7.3 μg/mL solution for the matrilin-3 group.
Add 10 μL of 10 μg/mL TGF-β1 to 45 μL of H2O to make a 1.8 μg/mL solution for the TGF-β1 group.
Mix 40 μL of 10 μg/mL matrilin-3 and 10 μL of 10 μg/mL TGF-β1, then add 5 μL of 1 mg/mL JBNts to make a mixed solution for the JBNm group.
Agitate the mixture to ensure proper mixing for each group.
Measure the absorption spectrum of each group using a spectrophotometer.
Add 160 μL of 10 mg/mL matrilin-3 to 640 μL of H2O to make an 800 μL solution for the matrilin-3 alone group.
Mix 160 μL of 10 μg/mL matrilin-3 with 40 μL of 10 μg/mL TGF-β1, then add it to 600 μL of H2O resulting in an 800 μL solution for the matrilin-3/TGF-β1 compound group.
Mix 160 μL of 10 μg/mL matrilin-3 and 40 μL of 10 μg/mL TGF-β1, then add 20 μL of 1 mg/mL JBNts to make an 800 μL solution for the full layer-by-layer JBNm group.
Measure the zeta-potential values for the three groups.
Insert two grids into a plasma cleaner for cleaning before negative staining.
Create a 200 µg/mL JBNt solution by mixing 10 µL of 1 mg/mL JBNts with 40 µL of distilled water.
Mix 30 µL of 100 µg/mL matrilin-3 with 20 µL of 100 µg/mL TGF-β1 and pipette several times.
Add 10 µL of 1 mg/mL JBNts to the matrilin-3/TGF-β1 mixture and pipette repeatedly.
Add 3 µL of the JBNt solution (200 µg/mL) on a grid for TEM analysis.
Add 3 µL of the JBNm solution on another grid for TEM analysis.
Leave grids with added solutions for 2 minutes.
Rinse each grid with 100 µL of uranyl acetate solution (0.5%).
Use filter papers to remove excess uranyl acetate from the grids.
Allow grids to air dry before TEM observation.
Operate a transmission electron microscope to observe and characterize samples.
Label TGF-β1 using a protein labeling kit following manufacturer's instructions.
Add 20 µL of 20 µg/mL labeled TGF-β1 to 25 µL of H2O to make an 8.9 µg/mL test solution.
Label matrilin-3 using a separate labeling kit.
Add 20 µL of 80 µg/mL labeled matrilin-3 to 25 µL of H2O to make a 36 µg/mL test solution.
Mix 20 µL of 80 µg/mL labeled matrilin-3 with 20 µL of 20 µg/mL labeled TGF-β1 and 5 µL of H2O, resulting in a labeled TGF-β1/matrilin-3 compound.
Pipette the mixture several times to mix thoroughly.
Add 5 µL of 1 mg/mL JBNts to 40 µL of H2O, resulting in an 111 µg/mL solution.
Mix 20 µL of 20 µg/mL labeled TGF-β1 with 20 µL of 80 µg/mL labeled matrilin-3 and pipette several times to mix thoroughly.
Add 5 µL of 1 mg/mL JBNts to the labeled TGF-β1/matrilin-3 solution, and pipette repeatedly to properly mix the compound.
Add 1.25 µL of 1 mg/mL JBNts to 198.75 µL of distilled water, resulting in a 6.25 µg/mL solution.
Add 10 µL of 10 µg/mL matrilin-3 to 190 µL of distilled water, resulting in a 0.5 µg/mL solution.
Add 2.5 µL of 10 µg/mL TGF-β1 to 197.5 µl of distilled water, resulting in a 0.125 µg/mL solution.
Mix 10 µL of 10 µg/ml matrilin-3 with 2.5 µL of 10 µg/ml TGF-β1 and pipette repeatedly to form JBNm group solution.
Add 1.25 µL of JBNts with a concentration of 1 mg/mL to the mixture solution and pipette.
Add 186.25 µL of distilled water to result in a 200 µL JBNm solution.
Use 200 µL of distilled water for the control group.
Place each sample group into their own well of a No. 1.5 chambered coverglass.
Store the coverglasses at -80 °C freezer for 1 h.
Freeze-dry the samples with a lyophilizer instrument.
Seed human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs) and human chondrocyte cells (10,000 cells per well) into each well of the prepared chambered coverglasses.
Incubate the two coverglasses for 4 h in a 37 °C incubator.
Aspirate the cell culture medium from the wells.
Rinse twice with PBS.
Fix cells with 4% paraformaldehyde for 5 min.
Remove and rinse samples with PBS.
Rinse the sample a second time to completely remove the 4% paraformaldehyde.
Incubate cells with 100 μL of 0.1% Triton-X for 10 min.
Wash cells with PBS.
Add 100 μL of 0.165 µM rhodamine-phalloidin to each well.
Wait for 30 min.
Wash cells with PBS again.
Add 0.1 µg/mL DAPI to each well to stain the nuclei.
Wait for 5 min.
Rinse wells with PBS twice.
Use a spectral confocal microscope to observe cell morphology and capture fluorescent images.
Open image processing software and load images.
Add a scale bar and calibrate the software.
Count the number of cells in a given area for each sample.
Use measuring tool to collect data on cell morphology for each sample.
Prepare three untreated 96-well plates.
Add five groups of samples to each plate.
For the JBNt group, add 3.75 µL of 1 mg/mL JBNts to 596.25 µL of distilled water.
Mix well to achieve a solution concentration of 6.25 µg/mL.
For the TGF-β1 group, add 7.5 µL of 10 µg/mL TGF-β1 to 592.5 µL of distilled water.
Mix well to achieve a test solution concentration of 0.125 µg/mL.
For the matrilin-3 group, add 30 µL of 10 µg/mL matrilin-3 to 570 µL of distilled water.
Mix well to achieve a test solution concentration of 0.5 µg/mL.
For the JBNm group, mix 7.5 µL of 10 µg/mL TGF-β1 with 30 µL of 10 µg/mL matrilin-3 and pipette several times.
Add 3.75 µL of 1 mg/mL JBNts to the solution.
Dilute JBNm solution with 558.75 µL of distilled water to obtain final concentrations.
Divide each sample group into six wells containing 100 µL per well.
Place plates containing samples into a -80 °C freezer for 1 h.
Freeze-dry samples using a lyophilizing instrument.
Seed hMSCs onto plates, with each well receiving 100 µL cell suspension (5,000 cells).
Incubate the three plates at 37 °C for 1 day, 3 days, or 5 days in 5% CO2.
Add 10 µL of CCK-8 solution to each well with cells and incubate at 37 °C for 2 h.
Measure absorption values of each well using a multi-mode microplate reader at 450 nm.
Seed a known gradient of hMSCs onto a 96-well plate and incubate for 4 h.
Use CCK-8 assay to measure the absorption values of the known number of cells.
Generate a standard curve based on cell numbers.
Calculate cell proliferation using the absorption standard curve.
Prepare 2% agarose by adding 400 mg of agarose powder to 20 mL of PBS.
Heat mixture up to 100 °C to completely dissolve agarose powder.
Combine 10 µL of 10 µg/mL TGF-β1 with the solution.
Mix 40 µL of 10 µg/mL matrilin-3 into the solution.
Add 5 µL of 1 mg/mL JBNts to the mixture.
Combine this solution with 250 µL of 2% agarose, creating the JBNm hydrogel.
Add 500 µL of PBS as a release solution.
Change the release solution every 3 days.
Keep each released solution for analysis.
Let the sample sit for 15 days.
Use an ELISA kit to test the captured release solutions according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Subtract the amount of TGF-β1 released in the PBS from the theoretical loading value to determine the remaining amount of TGF-β1.
Prepare seven groups of samples with each containing 20 µL of cell suspension (4 x 10^4 cells).
For the TGF-β1 group, add 5 µL of 10 µg/mL TGF-β1 to 25 µL of PBS resulting in a 1.6 µg/mL solution.
For the matrilin-3 group, add 20 µL of 10 µg/mL matrilin-3 to 10 µL of PBS resulting in a 6.7 µg/mL solution.
For the JBNt group, add 2.5 µL of 1 mg/mL JBNts to 27.5 µL of PBS resulting in an 83.3 µg/mL solution.
For the J/T/M JBNm group, mix 10 µL of matrilin-3 with 5 µL of TGF-β1.
Add 2.5 µL of JBNts to the mixed solution.
Dilute this mixture by adding 2.5 µL of PBS.
Use 30 μL of PBS as the sample for each control group.
Add 0.5 mL of cell culture medium to each well and replace it every 3 days.
For the positive control group, use a commercially available hMSC chondrogenic medium containing added TGF-β1.
For one negative control group, use a commercial hMSC chondrogenic medium without TGF-β1.
For another negative control group, use DMEM cell culture medium with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS).
Culture all samples for 15 days.
Extract the samples' RNA and perform PCR to study differentiation as described previously.
Prepare seven agarose-based samples in the same way as the cell differentiation with PCR method section.
Culture these prepared samples for 15 days.
Fix the samples with 4% formaldehyde for 1 day.
Soak the fixed samples in a 30% sucrose solution overnight.
Freeze the samples overnight at -80 °C using liquid nitrogen.
Fix the samples using optimal cutting temperature compound (OCT) reagent at -10 °C.
Operate a cryostat microtome to obtain 20 μm thick frozen sections of each sample.
Stain each section with an Anti-Collagen X antibody at a dilution of 1:800.
Dilute the fluorescent labeling secondary antibody in PBS.
Incubate the sections with the diluted secondary antibody according to the manufacturer's protocols.
Observe each section using a confocal microscope.
Use an excitation wavelength of 488 nm for observation.
Set the magnification to 40x on the eyepiece for detailed viewing.
